es.term: Náuseas y vómitos inducidos por quimioterapia (NVIC)
es.summary: Las NVIC son una reacción adversa frecuente a los agentes quimioterapéuticos, provocada por la estimulación del centro del vómito y la zona quimiorreceptora.
key_points: Se clasifican en anticipatoria, aguda, tardía y de ruptura.
Factores de riesgo: sexo femenino, <50 años, historia previa de NVIC, deshidratación.
El manejo combina antieméticos de diferentes clases y medidas no farmacológicas.
El desequilibrio electrolítico es una complicación frecuente.

pathophysiology: Los fármacos quimioterapéuticos liberan mediadores que estimulan la zona quimiorreceptora (CTZ).
Activación de receptores de serotonina (5‑HT3), dopamina y neuroquinina en el centro del vómito.
Se genera una señal motora que desencadena náuseas y contracciones del músculo liso gastrointestinal.
risk_factors: Historia previa de NVIC o náuseas durante el embarazo.
Uso de regímenes de quimioterapia altamente emetogénicos.
signs_symptoms: Sensación de náuseas persistente o intermitente.
Vómitos de contenido gástrico, a veces con sangre si hay irritación.
Pérdida de apetito y posible deshidratación.
diagnostics: Historia clínica enfocada en patrón de NVIC (anticipatoria, aguda, tardía).
Evaluación de hidratación: presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca, turgencia cutánea.
Laboratorio: electrolitos (Na+, K+, Cl-) y glucosa; valores fuera de rango indican complicación.
treatment: Antagonistas de 5‑HT3 (ondansetrón, granisetrón) – bloquean receptores periféricos y centrales.
Corticoides (dexametasona) – potencian la acción antiemética y reducen inflamación.
Antagonistas de neuroquinina (aprepitant) – inhiben la vía NK1 del centro del vómito.
Antihistamínicos y fenotiazinas (prometazina) para NVIC de bajo riesgo.
Hidratación intravenosa con solución salina isotónica.
complications: Reducción de la adherencia al esquema quimioterapéutico.
nursing_care: Evaluar frecuencia, intensidad (escala 0‑10) y patrón de NVIC cada 4 h.
Monitorear signos de deshidratación y registrar electrolitos.
Administrar antieméticos según orden, observar efectos adversos.
Mantener al paciente en posición semi‑sentada para reducir riesgo de aspiración.
Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos.
patient_teaching: Tomar antieméticos antes de iniciar la quimioterapia y según indicaciones.
Beber pequeños sorbos de líquidos claros cada 15‑30 min.
Evitar olores fuertes y alimentos grasos que pueden desencadenar náuseas.
Reportar vómitos persistentes o signos de deshidratación al personal de salud.
Utilizar técnicas de relajación (respiración profunda, música) para disminuir la ansiedad.

outcomes: Control de náuseas: paciente reporta intensidad ≤ 2/10 en escala de 0‑10 en 24 h.
Hidratación adecuada: ingesta oral ≥ 1500 mL/día y peso estable.

interventions.action: Administrar antiemético 5‑HT3 antes de la quimioterapia según prescripción.
interventions.rationale: Previene la estimulación de receptores serotoninérgicos en el CTZ.

interventions.action: Evaluar intensidad de náuseas cada 4 h usando escala numérica.
interventions.rationale: Permite ajustar la terapia y medir la efectividad del tratamiento.

interventions.action: Ofrecer líquidos claros en pequeños sorbos cada 15 min.
interventions.rationale: Mantiene hidratación y reduce irritación gástrica.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnicas de respiración diafragmática y distracción.
interventions.rationale: Disminuye la respuesta ansiosa que potencia la náusea.

interventions.action: Registrar y reportar cualquier vómito persistente o sangre en el contenido.
interventions.rationale: Identifica complicaciones que requieren intervención médica.

outcomes: Electrolitos (Na+, K+, Cl-) dentro de rangos normales en 48 h.
Signos de hidratación adecuados (PA 110/70 mmHg, turgencia cutánea presente).

interventions.action: Monitorear peso diario y balance hídrico (ingesta‑salida).
interventions.rationale: Detecta pérdidas de líquidos que pueden alterar electrolitos.

interventions.action: Obtener muestra de sangre para electrolitos cada 24 h mientras haya vómitos.
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar y corregir desequilibrios tempranamente.

interventions.action: Administrar solución salina isotónica IV según orden.
interventions.rationale: Reemplaza líquidos y electrolitos perdidos por vómitos.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre la importancia de ingerir alimentos ricos en potasio (plátano, papaya).
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a mantener niveles de potasio dentro del rango normal.

interventions.action: Evaluar signos de hiponatremia o hipopotasemia (confusión, debilidad muscular).
interventions.rationale: Facilita la detección precoz de complicaciones electrolíticas.

en.summary: CINV is a common adverse reaction to chemotherapeutic agents, caused by stimulation of the vomiting center and the chemoreceptor trigger zone.
key_points: They are classified as anticipatory, acute, delayed, and breakthrough.
Risk factors: female sex, <50 years, prior CINV history, dehydration.
Management combines antiemetics of different classes and non‑pharmacologic measures.
Electrolyte imbalance is a frequent complication.

pathophysiology: Chemotherapeutic drugs release mediators that stimulate the chemoreceptor trigger zone (CTZ).
Activation of serotonin (5‑HT3), dopamine, and neurokinin receptors in the vomiting center.
A motor signal is generated that triggers nausea and gastrointestinal smooth muscle contractions.
risk_factors: Prior CINV history or nausea during pregnancy.
Use of highly emetogenic chemotherapy regimens.
signs_symptoms: Vomiting of gastric contents, sometimes with blood if irritation occurs.
Loss of appetite and possible dehydration.
diagnostics: Focused history on CINV pattern (anticipatory, acute, delayed).
Hydration assessment: blood pressure, heart rate, skin turgor.
Laboratory: electrolytes (Na+, K+, Cl-) and glucose; out‑of‑range values indicate complication.
treatment: 5‑HT3 antagonists (ondansetron, granisetron) – block peripheral and central receptors.
Corticosteroids (dexamethasone) – enhance antiemetic action and reduce inflammation.
Neurokinin‑1 antagonists (aprepitant) – inhibit the NK1 pathway in the vomiting center.
Antihistamines and phenothiazines (promethazine) for low‑risk CINV.
Intravenous hydration with isotonic saline solution.
nursing_care: Assess frequency, intensity (0‑10 scale), and CINV pattern every 4 h.
Monitor dehydration signs and record electrolytes.
Administer antiemetics as ordered, observe adverse effects.
Keep patient in semi‑upright position to reduce aspiration risk.
patient_teaching: Take antiemetics before starting chemotherapy and as directed.
Drink small sips of clear liquids every 15‑30 min.
Avoid strong odors and greasy foods that may trigger nausea.
Report persistent vomiting or dehydration signs to health staff.
Use relaxation techniques (deep breathing, music) to reduce anxiety.

outcomes: Nausea control: patient reports intensity ≤ 2/10 on 0‑10 scale within 24 h.
Adequate hydration: oral intake ≥ 1500 mL/day and stable weight.

interventions.action: Administer 5‑HT3 antiemetic before chemotherapy per prescription.
interventions.rationale: Prevents stimulation of serotonergic receptors in the CTZ.

interventions.action: Assess nausea intensity every 4 h using a numeric scale.
interventions.rationale: Allows therapy adjustment and measures treatment effectiveness.

interventions.action: Offer clear liquids in small sips every 15 min.
interventions.rationale: Maintains hydration and reduces gastric irritation.

interventions.action: Teach diaphragmatic breathing and distraction techniques.
interventions.rationale: Reduces anxious response that amplifies nausea.

interventions.action: Document and report any persistent vomiting or blood in the content.
interventions.rationale: Identifies complications requiring medical intervention.

outcomes: Electrolytes (Na+, K+, Cl-) within normal ranges in 48 h.
Adequate hydration signs (BP 110/70 mmHg, present skin turgor).

interventions.action: Monitor daily weight and fluid balance (intake‑output).
interventions.rationale: Detects fluid losses that may alter electrolytes.

interventions.action: Obtain blood sample for electrolytes every 24 h while vomiting persists.
interventions.rationale: Identifies and corrects imbalances early.

interventions.action: Administer isotonic saline IV as ordered.
interventions.rationale: Replaces fluids and electrolytes lost with vomiting.

interventions.action: Educate patient on importance of eating potassium‑rich foods (banana, papaya).
interventions.rationale: Helps maintain potassium within normal range.

interventions.action: Assess signs of hyponatremia or hypokalemia (confusion, muscle weakness).
interventions.rationale: Facilitates early detection of electrolyte complications.

key_points.1.quote: Risk factors for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting include female sex, clients who experienced nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, age less than 50 years, and incidence of nausea and vomiting with previous chemotherapy treatments.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Risk factors for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting include female sex, clients who experienced nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, age less than 50 years, and incidence of nausea and vomiting with previous chemotherapy treatments.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Risk factors for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting include female sex, clients who experienced nausea and vomiting during pregnancy, age less than 50 years, and incidence of nausea and vomiting with previous chemotherapy treatments.

sections.risk_factors.2.quote: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalances are also associated with increased nausea and vomiting.

sections.diagnostics.0.quote: Nausea and vomiting may occur as anticipatory, beginning before a treatment begins, or during or soon after a treatment.

sections.treatment.2.quote: Aprepitant, a substance P/NK 1 receptor antagonist, crosses the blood-brain barrier to block neurokinin action in the CTZ, with peripheral effects in the GI tract to combat nausea and vomiting.

sections.treatment.4.quote: Clients may require transfusions of packed red blood cells, hydration with isotonic intravenous fluids, and oxygen.

sections.complications.0.quote: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalances are also associated with increased nausea and vomiting.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: The age of the client should be carefully considered prior to administering antiemetics, specifically in older adults and pediatric clients due to their potential adverse effects.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Granisetron ( Kytril ) IV: 10 mcg/kg infused starting 30 minutes before chemotherapy; repeat at 4 and 8 hours.
